hints: Focus on what type of functional group reacts with sodium metal to release hydrogen gas.
Remember that only alcohols and carboxylic acids contain the acidic $\text{O-H}$ group that reacts with $\text{Na}$, so narrow your list to the alcohols first.
Now check which of those alcohols can actually be oxidised, recalling that tertiary alcohols resist oxidation because there is no hydrogen on the carbon bearing the $\text{OH}$.
walkthrough:
**Use the sodium test to find the functional group**

Reaction with sodium to give hydrogen is a test for an acidic proton in an $\text{O-H}$ group. This tells us T must be an alcohol (or a carboxylic acid).

$$2\text{ROH} + 2\text{Na} \rightarrow 2\text{RONa} + \text{H}_2$$

**Use oxidation to narrow it down further**

Hot, acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ oxidises primary alcohols to carboxylic acids and secondary alcohols to ketones. Tertiary alcohols are not oxidised because the carbon attached to $\text{OH}$ has no hydrogen to remove.

**Check each compound**

Option A, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$, is butan-2-ol, a secondary alcohol. It has an $\text{O-H}$ so it reacts with $\text{Na}$, and it has one H on the $\text{C-OH}$ so it is oxidised to a ketone. This fits both observations perfectly.

options.A: Correct. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$ is a secondary alcohol. It reacts with sodium via its $\text{O-H}$ group to give $\text{H}_2$, and it is oxidised by hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ to the ketone butanone.
options.B: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CHO}$ is an aldehyde. It is oxidised to a carboxylic acid, but it has no $\text{O-H}$ group so it does not react with sodium to give hydrogen. Students who focus only on oxidation may pick this trap.
options.C: Incorrect. $(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{COH}$ is a tertiary alcohol. It does react with sodium to give hydrogen, but it resists oxidation by $\text{KMnO}_4$ because the carbon bearing the $\text{OH}$ has no hydrogen atom to lose.
options.D: Incorrect. $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_3$ is a ketone. Ketones are not oxidised by hot acidified $\text{KMnO}_4$ under these conditions, and with no $\text{O-H}$ group it does not react with sodium. It fails both tests.
